description.summary: place surfaces in the side canvas

protocol.description:
The side canvas is a column that slides in over the desktop from the right edge of an output. The compositor owns the column: where it sits, when it is shown and how it moves. Clients place surfaces in it as items.
Items are stacked top to bottom by their order (set_order, version 3), and in the order they were created where that is the same, each at the full width of the column. The compositor chooses the width and tells the client through configure; the client chooses the height through the size of the buffer it attaches.
The canvas is shown and hidden by the user. A client may also ask for it to be shown (show, version 3), without taking the keyboard. Clients are told when the canvas shows and hides so they can pause work nobody can see.
The compositor also opens the canvas when a drag and drop operation rests at the right edge of an output, so an item can take the drop, and tells every manager when a drag starts and ends (version 4), so a client can put an item in the column that is ready for it.
The column has a fixed height, and items share it (version 5): each tells the compositor how tall its content is, and the compositor tells each how tall it may be, so every item keeps a share of the column and scrolls what does not fit.

interface.name: otto_canvas_manager_v1

description.summary: creates canvas items

interface.description: The manager global lets a client put surfaces in the side canvas.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface already has a role

request.name: get_canvas_item

description.summary: place a surface in the canvas

request.description:
Give the surface the canvas item role and add it to the column, below the items with the same or a lower order. A new item has order 0.
It is a protocol error (role) to pass a surface that already has another role.
The compositor answers with a configure event. The client must acknowledge it before it attaches a buffer. From version 5 a max_height event follows the first configure. A visibility event (shown or hidden) comes next.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager

request.description: Destroy the manager object. Items already created are unaffected.

event.name: drag_mime_type

description.summary: a type the starting drag offers

event.description: Sent once for each mime type the data of a starting drag and drop operation is offered as, right before drag_started. There may be none when the source has not said yet; the client should then treat what the drag carries as unknown.

arg.name: mime_type
arg.summary: a mime type the drag offers

event.name: drag_started

description.summary: a drag and drop operation began

event.description:
A drag and drop operation began somewhere in the session, from any client. The drag_mime_type events sent since the last drag_started or drag_ended list what it offers.
While it goes on, the compositor opens the canvas when the pointer rests at the right edge of an output, the way show does: the keyboard does not move. A client with nothing in the canvas may add an item now, to be there when it opens. Items take the drop through wl_data_device like any other surface.

event.name: drag_ended

description.summary: the drag and drop operation ended

event.description:
The drag and drop operation announced by drag_started ended, with a drop anywhere or cancelled. A client whose item the drop landed on has had wl_data_device.drop before this event.
If the drag opened the canvas and the drop did not land on an item, the canvas hides again.

interface.name: otto_canvas_item_v1

description.summary: a surface in the side canvas

interface.description:
One surface in the column. The compositor positions it; the client draws it at the configured width and at whatever height it needs. Content taller than the space left in the column is clipped.
From version 5 the column's height is shared: the client says how tall its content is with set_content_height, and the compositor answers with max_height, the most the item may be tall. A client that keeps to it is never clipped.
Destroying the item removes the surface from the canvas. The surface keeps its role and may only be given to a new canvas item.
An item gets the keyboard when the user presses on it, or when the canvas is shown if it asked for that with set_keyboard_interactivity (version 2). An item that set never (version 3) gets it in neither case. While an item has the keyboard the compositor passes Escape to it rather than hiding the canvas itself, so the item decides what Escape means; an item that has nothing else to do with it should send dismiss. When the canvas hides, the keyboard goes back to whoever had it before an item took it.

entry.name: invalid_keyboard_interactivity
entry.summary: the keyboard interactivity value is not in the enum

enum.name: keyboard_interactivity

description.summary: when the item takes the keyboard

enum.description: Whether the item is given the keyboard as the canvas comes on screen.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: the item gets the keyboard only when the user presses on it

entry.name: on_show
entry.summary: the item gets the keyboard when the canvas is shown

entry.name: never
entry.summary: the item never gets the keyboard, not even when pressed on

event.name: configure

description.summary: the width to draw at

event.description:
The width, in logical points, the item is laid out at. It is the width of the canvas column, and changes when the user changes it.
The client acknowledges with ack_configure and draws its next buffer at this width. The height is the client's choice.

event.name: shown

description.summary: the canvas is on screen

event.description: The canvas is visible, or on its way in. The item receives frame callbacks and should draw current content.

event.name: hidden

description.summary: the canvas is off screen

event.description: The canvas is off screen. The item receives no frame callbacks until the next shown event, and may stop work that only feeds what it draws.

request.name: ack_configure

description.summary: acknowledge a configure

request.description: Acknowledge the configure event with the given serial.

request.name: set_keyboard_interactivity

description.summary: take the keyboard when the canvas is shown

request.description:
Say whether the item takes the keyboard when the canvas is shown. The default is none.
With on_show, the compositor gives the item the keyboard once the canvas has settled open, from a toggle or a swipe, unless another item already has it. When several items ask for it, the first one in the column gets it. The change applies from the next time the canvas is shown.
With never, the item takes no keyboard at all: presses on it reach it as pointer events and the keyboard stays where it was, so the app the user is working in keeps its focus, selection and caret. This applies at once.
It is a protocol error (invalid_keyboard_interactivity) to pass a value that is not in the keyboard_interactivity enum, or never on an object of version 2.

arg.name: interactivity
arg.summary: when the item takes the keyboard

request.name: dismiss

description.summary: hide the canvas

request.description: Ask the compositor to hide the canvas, for example after the user acted on something in the item. Ignored while the canvas is hidden.

request.name: show

description.summary: show the canvas

request.description:
Ask the compositor to show the canvas, sliding it in on the output under the pointer, for example because the item has something new the user should see. Ignored while the canvas is shown or following the user's fingers, while the session is locked and while the compositor has the canvas set aside for another view (such as an overview of the windows); ask again on the next change.
The keyboard does not move: no item is given it on this show, even one that set on_show, so the app the user is working in keeps it. The canvas then stays open until the user hides it, or an item sends dismiss. Until the user acts on the canvas, a press outside it still reaches what is under the pointer, and the canvas hides when that button is released outside it; Escape goes to the app with the keyboard.

request.name: set_order

description.summary: where the item sits in the column

request.description: Set the item's place in the column. Items with a lower order sit higher; items with the same order sit in the order they were created. The default is 0, and a negative order puts the item above the items that never set one. The column is laid out again at once.

request.name: set_content_height

description.summary: how tall the item's content is

request.description:
Say how tall, in logical points, the item would be with room for all of its content: its natural height, however tall that is, not the height it is drawn at. Send it before the first buffer and again whenever it changes.
The compositor shares the column's height among the items by what they ask for and answers with max_height. Until an item has sent one, the compositor counts it at the height of its buffer.

event.name: max_height

description.summary: the most the item may be tall

event.description:
The most, in logical points, the item may be tall, so that it and the items around it fit in the column. The client draws its next buffer no taller than the smaller of this and its content's height, and scrolls whatever does not fit.
An item whose content fits in its share is given its content's height. Items that want more share what is left equally, and every item keeps a share of the column, however tall the others are, unless the column is too short to give each one a useful height.
Sent after the first configure, before shown, and again whenever the share changes: an item's content height changes, items come, go or move, or the column changes size or moves to another output. The client should resize promptly, since items stack by the height of their buffers.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: remove the item

request.description: Remove the surface from the canvas. The items below it move up.
